findings.title: Result artifact lacks a run date/timestamp
findings.message: The artifact records the host and source_commit but no timestamp of when the manual run was performed, so a re-run against the same commit (or on a patched build) cannot be distinguished from the original run when comparing results over time.
findings.suggestion: Add a top-level "recorded_at" field with the ISO-8601 timestamp of the run (and optionally the operator name) next to "source_commit".

findings.title: No overall result field despite a non-passing sub-check
findings.message: The file records five passing checklist items but also a non-passing desktop drag attempt, with no top-level verdict indicating whether item-1 overall passed or whether the drag failure is blocking. Consumers must cross-read multiple fields to infer the outcome, which invites misinterpretation.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit top-level outcome field next to the checklist (e.g. "overall_result": "pass" or "fail") plus a short notes field stating whether the desktop drag failure is blocking.

fix.after:
"suite_revision": 2,
  "overall_result": "pass",
  "overall_notes": "All five checklist checks passed; desktop drag attempt produced no object change and is recorded as not passed (non-blocking).",

findings.title: desktop_drag_attempt conflates observation and verdict in one free-text string
findings.message: The value mixes a factual observation ('no object change') with a verdict ('not passed') in a single free-text string, and its type (string) is inconsistent with the sibling "native_keyboard_placement" object. Any tooling that aggregates these results must substring-match prose instead of reading a field, and formatting tweaks will silently break that matching.
findings.suggestion: Split the string into structured fields so the verdict is machine-readable, e.g. {"object_change": false, "passed": false}.

finding.title: Drag-based checklist passes are not instrumentally corroborated
finding.message: Checklist steps 1, 2, 4, and 5 all specifically verify mouse-drag behavior (drag placement, held-state geometry, drop rejection, drag cancellation), but the tool's own drag attempts failed (lines 20-22), the tool only verified the final state, and the final state (one block, Undo 1 / Redo 0) is indistinguishable from a keyboard-Return placement such as the one the tool itself performed earlier. The recording of “All five checks passed” therefore rests entirely on operator self-report, not on native inspection, and the markdown does not make that limitation explicit in the acceptance sentence.
finding.suggestion: State explicitly that four of the five checks (the drag-dependent ones) are operator-attested and not instrumentally corroborated, and that the final native state is consistent with either a mouse drag or keyboard placement, e.g. append: “Checks 1, 2, 4 and 5 depend on mouse-drag behavior that the tool could not deliver or observe; their pass status is operator-attested only, and the final state does not distinguish a drag placement from a keyboard placement.”
finding.evidence:
The user reported “All five checks passed”. Final native inspection independently
showed exactly one selected Block (block-2, 80 × 50), Undo 1 / Redo 0, rejection
off and Connector focused after cancellation.
